description: Set up an isolated Python virtual environment for a data analysis project. The project is located at /home/ga/workspace/sales_analysis/ and contains a requirements.txt file with specific package versions (pandas==1.5.3, numpy==1.23.5, matplotlib==3.6.0). Your global Python has conflicting versions installed. You must: (1) Create a virtual environment named 'venv' in the project root directory /home/ga/workspace/sales_analysis/venv using 'python3 -m venv venv', (2) Activate the virtual environment with 'source venv/bin/activate', (3) Install all dependencies from requirements.txt using 'pip install -r requirements.txt', (4) Configure VSCode to use the venv interpreter by either using Command Palette 'Python: Select Interpreter' and selecting the venv interpreter, OR by creating/editing .vscode/settings.json in the project to set 'python.defaultInterpreterPath' to point to the venv Python (either absolute path '/home/ga/workspace/sales_analysis/venv/bin/python' or relative '${workspaceFolder}/venv/bin/python'). The main Python script analyze_sales.py should be able to run without import errors once the environment is properly configured.
